items.example_en: The whole family was there.

items.example: Mis padres viven en el campo.
items.example_en: My parents live in the countryside.
items.note: False friend risk: los parientes means relatives, not parents.

items.example: Mi hermano es más joven que yo.
items.example_en: My brother is younger than me.
items.note: los hermanos covers brothers, or siblings in general.

items.example_en: Their son started school.
items.note: los hijos means children, la hija is daughter.

items.example: Vamos a casa de mis abuelos el domingo.
items.example_en: We're going to my grandparents' on Sunday.
My nephew is turning five.
items.note: la sobrina is niece; el primo and la prima are cousins.

items.example: Mi marido cocina mejor que yo.
items.example_en: My husband cooks better than I do.
items.note: mi mujer or mi esposa is my wife.

items.example: Vivo con mi pareja desde el año pasado.
items.example_en: I've lived with my partner since last year.
items.note: Feminine noun regardless of the partner's gender.

items.example: Está soltero desde hace un año.
items.example_en: He's been single for a year.
items.note: estar soltero, not ser: it is a state that can change.

items.example: Están casados desde hace diez años.
items.example_en: They've been married for ten years.
items.note: Agrees: casada, casados, casadas.

items.example: Es un amigo íntimo de la familia.
items.example_en: He's a close friend of the family.
items.note: íntimo here means close, not intimate in a romantic sense.

items.example: Me llevo muy bien con mi hermana.
items.example_en: I get along really well with my sister.
items.note: Reflexive, and the pronoun changes with the subject.

items.example_en: She's tall and slim.
items.note: Adjectives agree in gender and number: alta, altos, altas.

items.example: Tiene el pelo castaño y corto.
items.example_en: He has short brown hair.
items.note: Spanish says he HAS the hair, with the definite article.

items.example: Tiene los ojos verdes como su madre.
items.example_en: She has green eyes like her mother.
My colleague wears round glasses.
items.note: In Latin America: lentes or anteojos.

items.example: Se parece mucho a su padre.
items.example_en: She looks a lot like her father.
items.note: Reflexive and always with a.

items.example: Un señor de mediana edad preguntó por ti.
items.example_en: A middle-aged man asked for you.
items.note: de plus a quality describes people: de ojos claros, de buen humor.

items.example_en: The neighbour is very nice.
items.note: False friend: it does not mean sympathetic, which is comprensivo.

items.example_en: Your brother is really funny.
items.note: False friend: not gracious. divertido also means fun.

items.example_en: It's a very hard-working team.
items.note: Feminine trabajadora.

items.example_en: He's as stubborn as a mule.
items.note: Also cabezota, more colloquial.

items.english: to be in a good mood
items.example_en: She's in a good mood today.
items.note: estar for the passing mood; ser for the permanent character.

items.example: A pesar de todo, tiene buen carácter.
items.example_en: In spite of everything, she's even-tempered.
items.note: un personaje is a character in a story.

items.example_en: I'm happy to see you.
items.note: estar for mood, ser feliz for a settled disposition.

items.example: El final de la película es triste.
items.example_en: The end of the film is sad.
items.note: The film IS sad (ser); you ARE sad right now (estar).

items.example: Estoy cansada, me voy a dormir.
items.example_en: I'm tired, I'm going to sleep.
items.note: ser cansado would mean you are tiring for others.

items.example_en: I'm afraid of flying.
items.note: Spanish HAS fear. Same pattern: tener hambre, sed, frío, calor, razón.

items.example_en: I'm fed up with this noise.
items.note: Common in speech, a bit blunt but not rude.

items.example_en: It makes me angry to arrive late.
items.note: Same backwards pattern as gustar: the thing is the subject.

items.example_en: He resigned? No way!
items.note: Negative command form, used purely as an exclamation.

items.example_en: You passed? How great!
items.note: qué plus adjective is the all-purpose exclamation.

items.example_en: It stopped raining. Thank goodness.
items.note: Literally less bad.

items.example_en: Are you coming? It depends on the time.
items.note: depender always takes de.

items.example_en: I'm fine, and you?
items.note: The cheapest way to keep a conversation going.

items.example_en: Anyway, we had a good time.
items.note: Wraps up a rambling story. Extremely common in speech.
